:::{#thm-bsc-capacity}
#### Capacity of the binary symmetric channel

The [binary symmetric channel](#def-binary-symmetric-channel)
with crossover probability $\epsilon$ has capacity

$$C = 1 - h(\epsilon) \text{ bits per channel use},$$

where $h$ is the [binary entropy function](#def-binary-entropy).
A uniformly distributed input achieves it.

:::

::: {.proof}

Fix any input distribution.
By [the definition of mutual information](entropy.qmd#def-mutual-information),

$$I(X; Y) = H(Y) - H(Y \mid X).$$

Given $X = x$, the output equals $x$ with probability $1 - \epsilon$
and differs from it with probability $\epsilon$,
so the [entropy of $Y$ given $X = x$](entropy.qmd#def-entropy-given-value)
is $h(\epsilon)$ for both inputs.
Averaging over $x$, the [conditional entropy](entropy.qmd#def-conditional-entropy)
is $H(Y \mid X) = h(\epsilon)$, whatever the input distribution.

$Y$ takes two values, so $H(Y) \le \log_2 2 = 1$ bit
[@cover2006elements, section 2.6].
Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
I(X; Y)
&= H(Y) - h(\epsilon) \\
&\le 1 - h(\epsilon).
\end{aligned}
$$

If $X$ is uniform on $\{0, 1\}$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\P(Y = 1)
&= \P(X = 0) \, \epsilon + \P(X = 1) \, (1 - \epsilon) \\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \epsilon + \tfrac{1}{2} (1 - \epsilon) \\
&= \tfrac{1}{2},
\end{aligned}
$$

so $H(Y) = 1$ bit and $I(X; Y) = 1 - h(\epsilon)$.
The bound is attained, so it is the maximum $C$.

:::
